A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAMF research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are available and readable, supporting reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on HateMM and MultiHateClip, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, qualitative examples, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds VLM comparisons, reasoning-quality measurements, text-only ablations, and full-pipeline efficiency results.

M1.justification: The three-stage reasoning process, encoders, LGCF, hierarchical SCA fusion, and classifier remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. Renaming adversarial reasoning to contrastive reasoning and disclosing its complete prompt do not establish a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate binary hateful-video detection using 1,083 HateMM videos and 959 Chinese/964 English MultiHateClip videos. The added experiments vary models and input configurations within retained coverage; Appendix A supplies dataset background rather than introducing another dataset or task.

E2.justification: The main Table 1 comparator set is retained after matching the HateMM/MHC naming. CMFusion is newly included in the efficiency comparison in Table 5. The additional reasoning generators principally extend RAMF component comparisons rather than the standalone detection baseline set.

E3.justification: v2 adds generator configurations, controlled text/description/full-reasoning comparisons, reasoning-output metrics, and full-pipeline latency, throughput, and memory measurements. The original splits and training budgets remain. The displayed CoT prompt also gains hate/offense definitions and interpersonal-conflict qualifications; unchanged ablation values do not establish that this comparison was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component ablations and sensitivity plots, v2 adds broader generator-capacity comparisons, reasoning-length and similarity analyses, controlled VLM substitutions on MHC-Chinese, and an ablation separating reasoning benefits from multimodal fusion. Appendix I adds two failure-case analyses, although their attribution to RAMF conflicts with the figures' baseline-model descriptions.

E5.justification: v1 reports standard deviations only for the HXP/CLAP/CLIP multimodal comparisons in appendix Table 4. v2 Table 1 substantially expands uncertainty reporting to existing unimodal, zero-shot, and other feature-configuration results. Five-fold evaluation and seed 2021 remain unchanged; additional runs or significance testing are not established.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 6–9 add substantial generator, efficiency, reasoning-quality, and text-only results, while most principal RAMF scores remain unchanged. Table 1 revises MHC-Chinese CLIP macro-F1 from 58.3 to 61.2 and removes most previously reported hate-class F1 entries. Table 2 retains its numerical values but reverses the accuracy/macro-F1 headings, creating inconsistent metric assignments.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 7 formally defines reasoning-contribution scores using softmax-normalized sums of attention received in the second SCA layer; v1 plotted contributions without this definition. The LGCF/SCA equations retain their substance, and neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same reasoning-plus-fusion contributions, two-benchmark generalization claim, and stated 3% macro-F1 and 7% hate-recall improvements. The adversarial-to-contrastive terminology change does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning generator capacity, semantic richness versus reasoning divergence, Chinese-context alignment, and reasoning benefits independent of multimodal fusion. It distinguishes offline reasoning from downstream inference cost and discusses failures involving conflicting modalities and pragmatic language. These are substantive additions, although the failure-case model attribution is inconsistent.

D1.justification: v2 adds the complete contrastive prompt, dataset provenance and annotation details, and explicit information about offline processing and full-pipeline efficiency measurement. Access instructions change from anonymous access/future release to a public GitHub repository pointer. Algorithm 1 and most training hyperparameters were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 substantially broadens positioning beyond VLM/CoT reasoning to local semantic learning, contrastive representations, intention modeling, and reverse-prompt contrastive decoding. It explicitly distinguishes RAMF's alternative semantic interpretations from distribution-level decoding. Additional citations cover these approaches, newer hateful-video work, and newly evaluated VLMs.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative order are retained. Changes include the reasoning terminology, a rewritten problem formulation with a separate framework overview, clearer notation explanations, expanded appendix organization, language corrections, and updated affiliations. Much of the expansion consists of new scientific material rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, substantially reorganizing its displays. Table 1 adopts mean-plus-deviation cells, Table 2 becomes four panels, three prompt figures are merged, and existing plots are redrawn or rearranged. New analysis tables, a full-prompt figure, and failure-case figures accompany retained architecture and qualitative displays.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through complete prompts, broader uncertainty reporting, diagnostic experiments, and explicit separation of 0.20 ms fusion inference from the reported 109.16 s full Qwen2.5-VL-32B pipeline. These gains are tempered by newly reversed metric headings in Table 2, conflicting assignments in Table 3, and ambiguous failure-case attribution. The clearer resource accounting and reproducibility support a limited net improvement, while these reporting problems constrain confidence in the expanded evidence.
